title: Free two-term cover of a complex
statement: Let $A$ be a ring and let $M^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. There exists a morphism $Q^\bullet \to M^\bullet$ that is degreewise surjective and surjective on cocycles in every degree, together with a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes $0 \to Q'^\bullet \to Q^\bullet \to Q''^\bullet \to 0$ in which $Q'^\bullet$ and $Q''^\bullet$ are direct sums of shifts $A[k]$ with zero differential.

proof.text: Construct the degree-n lower free module L_n = (M^n ->_0 A), and the degree-n upper module U_n = (M^(n-1) ->_0 A) times (Z^n(M) ->_0 A). Set Q^n=U_n times L_n. Its differential sends the lower factor into the first upper factor in degree n+1, using the canonical index equality (n+1)-1=n, and is zero on all upper factors. The next differential kills this image, so the square is zero. Send lower basis vectors to the elements indexing them, upper basis vectors to their differential in M, and cocycle basis vectors to the cocycles indexing them. The equalities d_M squared=0 and d_M(z)=0 prove that this evaluation commutes with differentials. The lower basis vector indexed by any element z in M^n proves degreewise surjectivity. These constructions and proofs are the private CoverLower, CoverUpper, coverD, coverD_sq, coverQ, coverUpperEval, coverEval, coverEval_comm and coverMap declarations.

For a cocycle z in degree n, take in Q^n the vector whose cocycle component is the single vector indexed by (z, d_M(z)=0), with coefficient 1, and whose other components are zero. The explicit cover differential kills it, and evaluation sends it to z. This proves surjectivity on cocycles by a real Lean calculation, retaining the degreewise surjectivity already proved.

Define zero-differential complexes Qprime^n=U_n and Qdoubleprime^n=L_n. The first-factor inclusion Qprime -> Q and second-factor projection Q -> Qdoubleprime are maps of complexes whose composite is zero. In each degree their projection and inclusion maps give a splitting; coverSplitting verifies the three splitting identities. Splitting.shortExact and HomologicalComplex.shortExact_of_degreewise_shortExact prove the resulting short complex short exact. Apply lem-pc-zero-differential-free-coproduct to the two endpoints: for U_n use the inverse of Finsupp.sumFinsuppLEquivProdFinsupp, giving basis M^(n-1) disjoint union Z^n(M), and for L_n use the identity free basis. The indices are sigma types of degree and basis element, with degree map Sigma.fst. This proves both coproduct descriptions with their prescribed universe.

lean.statement: theorem exists_freeComplexCover {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) : ∃ (S : ShortComplex (CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)) (f : S.X₂ ⟶ M), (∀ n : ℤ, Function.Surjective (f.f n)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℤ) (z : M.X n), M.d n (n + 1) z = 0 → ∃ x : S.X₂.X n, S.X₂.d n (n + 1) x = 0 ∧ f.f n x = z) ∧ S.ShortExact ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Nonempty (S.map (HomologicalComplex.eval (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)).Splitting) ∧ ∃ (I₁ I₃ : Type u) (d₁ : I₁ → ℤ) (d₃ : I₃ → ℤ), Nonempty (S.X₁ ≅ ∐ (fun i : I₁ => (HomologicalComplex.single (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (d₁ i)).obj (ModuleCat.of A A))) ∧ Nonempty (S.X₃ ≅ ∐ (fun i : I₃ => (HomologicalComplex.single (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (d₃ i)).obj (ModuleCat.of A A)))
